files.content:
# Todo List Application — Business Requirements and Constraints

## 1. Todo Item State Lifecycle

Every Todo item SHALL exist in exactly one of three business-defined states at any given time:
- "Active": Pending completion; actionable by the owner.
- "Completed": Marked finished by the actor who owns the item or by an admin. Immutable after completion.
- "Deleted": Marked removed and hidden from standard active lists, but retained for 30-day recovery period. Not immediately erased.

### 1.1 State Transitions (EARS Format)
- WHEN a user creates a Todo, THE item SHALL begin in the "Active" state.
- WHEN a user marks a Todo as completed, THE item SHALL move to "Completed".
- WHEN a user deletes a Todo, THE item SHALL move to "Deleted" and remain recoverable for a 30-day window.
- WHEN the 30-day retention ends, THE system SHALL permanently erase the item so it is inaccessible and non-recoverable.
- WHEN a Todo in "Deleted" is restored by owner or admin within 30 days, THE item SHALL return to "Active" with previous content.
- IF a user attempts to edit or complete a "Deleted" or "Completed" Todo, THEN THE system SHALL deny the action and show an actionable error.

### 1.2 State Transition Rules
- WHERE an item is "Deleted" but within retention, THE owner SHALL be permitted to restore to "Active".
- WHERE an item is "Completed", THE owner SHALL ONLY be able to view (not modify).

### 1.3 Mermaid Diagram: Todo Item Lifecycle
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Create Todo"] --> B["Active"]
  B -->|"User completes"| C["Completed"]
  B -->|"User deletes"| D["Deleted"]
  D -->|"Admin/user restores (within retention)"| B
  D -->|"Retention period ends"| E["Permanently Deleted"]
```

## 2. Validation Rules and Limits

### 2.1 Field Validation (EARS Format)
#### Title
- THE title field SHALL be mandatory for each Todo item.
- THE title SHALL consist of 1-100 characters of non-blank text.
- IF user submits empty or whitespace for title, THEN THE system SHALL reject the item creation/edit and display an error.
#### Description
- THE description field SHALL be optional.
- WHERE given, THE description SHALL be ≤ 1,000 characters.
#### Due Date
- WHERE provided, THE due date SHALL be a valid date in the future.
- IF not provided, THE Todo SHALL have no deadline.
- IF user tries to set a due date to a past date, THEN THE system SHALL deny with actionable error.

### 2.2 User-specific and Uniqueness Limits
- THE system SHALL allow a maximum of 1,000 Active Todos per user at any time.
- IF user at maximum, THEN THE system SHALL deny further creations and specify the reason.
- EACH Todo SHALL have a unique title among the user’s active Todos.
- EACH Todo SHALL be owned by one user; no shared ownership except by admin action in business-justified scenarios.

## 3. Operational Constraints (Business Only)

### 3.1 Ownership, Access, Permissions
- ONLY the Todo owner (or admins) SHALL have permission to modify, complete, or delete the Todo.
- Admins SHALL have access to all Todo items and all operations for compliance or support.
- WHERE a user deletes a Todo, THE item SHALL disappear from active lists and be visible only in deleted views (if product supports this).

### 3.2 Completion and Editing Restrictions
- IF a Todo is "Completed", THEN users SHALL be unable to re-complete or edit, but may view.
- IF a Todo is "Deleted", THEN no edits or completion permitted unless restored.

### 3.3 Retention, Archiving, Data Loss Prevention
- Deleted Todos SHALL be retained 30 days before permanent erasure.
- Restore operation during this window SHALL return status to "Active" with content preserved.
- AFTER 30 days, THE system SHALL permanently erase, disallowing all access.

### 3.4 Error Handling and Edge Cases
- IF user/admin acts outside permissions or state rules, THEN THE system SHALL report specific error per item.
- IN batch operations, THE system SHALL process permitted items, reject forbidden ones, and provide per-item error feedback.
- IF maintenance, system error, or rule failure occurs, THEN THE user SHALL see a clear, actionable message with no technical jargon.

## 4. Summary Table: States and Transitions
| State        | Possible Transitions                                        | Actors       |
|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|
| Active       | Complete, Delete                                           | Owner/Admin  |
| Completed    | View only                                                  | Owner/Admin  |
| Deleted      | Restore (≤30d), Permanent delete (after 30d)               | Owner/Admin  |
| Permanently Deleted | None                                                | System       |

## 5. Additional Business Rules

- All state transition, permission, and retention rules APPLY equally to bulk operations, with individual rule enforcement and error reporting.
- THE system SHALL audit all state changes for compliance and troubleshooting.

---

> All requirements herein must be interpreted as business needs. Technical details (schema, APIs, database) are defined in the next phase.

files.reason: To describe at a high level any external dependencies or integration requirements (e.g., email verification, analytics) in a natural language format.
files.content:
# External Integrations Requirements for todoApp

## Introduction
TodoApp is designed as a standalone service focusing on robust, reliable todo management. The service is intended to operate effectively with the absolute minimum of external dependencies, in alignment with the vision for simplicity, reliability, and privacy. This requirements specification details current and foreseeable integration requirements involving external third-party services—framed to ensure the service is both lean at launch and extensible for future business and user needs.

## Third-Party Service Integration Requirements
- WHEN the application is deployed for the first release, THE todoApp SHALL NOT depend on any third-party integrations for its core todo management functionality.
- WHERE functionality such as account registration or password recovery is required, THE todoApp SHALL support the option to integrate with an external transactional email service for delivering critical user notifications, such as account verification and password reset emails.
- IF legal compliance (such as audit logging or regulatory record-keeping) becomes a requirement, THEN THE todoApp SHALL be extensible to support integration with compliance or auditing platforms, ensuring all business rules and legal obligations can be satisfied.
- THE todoApp SHALL NOT implement or require analytic, advertisement, cloud storage, or push/SMS/in-app notification integrations for the minimum viable release.

## Conditional Email Notification Workflows
- WHEN users are required to verify their email account, AND email delivery is enabled, THE system SHALL send a verification email through a designated external transactional email service. Otherwise, the verification flow SHALL be completed without email notification.
- WHEN a user requests a password reset, AND email delivery is enabled, THE system SHALL transmit a one-time password reset link or token via a configured external email provider.
- THE only supported notifications in the minimum specification SHALL be user-initiated, critical events (account registration verification, password reset). No promotional or marketing notifications SHALL be supported.
- WHEN sending any critical notification, THE system SHALL log the notification transaction results (success/failure) for later troubleshooting and business audit purposes.

### Mermaid Diagram: Conditional Email Integration
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["User Registers or Requests Password Reset"] --> B{"Email Service Integration Enabled?"}
  B -->|"Yes"| C["Send Verification/Reset Email via Third-party Provider"]
  B -->|"No"| D["Complete Request without Email Notification"]
```

## Notification Requirements & Limitations
- THE todoApp SHALL operate without notification functionality if no integration is enabled.
- WHERE email delivery is supported and enabled, ONLY user-triggered notifications related to security or access SHALL be permitted.
- THE todoApp SHALL NOT support automated reminders, push notifications, SMS, or in-app notifications for the minimal product launch.
- THE service SHALL log the outcome of attempted notifications where implemented, enabling basic trouble analysis and business oversight.

## Data Security and Compliance for Integrations
- WHERE integration with external services is configured, THE todoApp SHALL require proper encryption and data-protection for any user information transmitted outside the core system, following industry best practice and local regulatory standards.
- WHEN a new integration is added, THE system SHALL undergo privacy and security review to assess risks and adherence to applicable compliance standards.
- WHERE external communication involves personal user data, consent and relevant notices SHALL be provided to users in accordance with prevailing privacy regulations.

## Future Integration Extensibility
- THE system architecture SHALL enable external service integrations to be added or removed at deployment time without impacting core functionality or causing service downtime.
- All business-critical data (such as todo items, users, and completion status) SHALL always be stored within the todoApp's own controlled data environment and protected independently of any third-party services.
- WHEN additional integrations for analytics, cloud storage, or authentication are required by new business needs, THE todoApp SHALL allow independent configuration of each integration so that disabling any integration does not compromise the ability to use or manage todos.
- THE service SHALL provide comprehensive documentation of all current and planned integrations in an external integration register for developer reference.

## Integration Principles and Governance
- Every external integration SHALL be optional, independently configurable, and must never be a runtime requirement for baseline use of the todo application.
- The todoApp's build and deployment pipeline SHALL allow for the enabling or disabling of integrations via configuration without changing business logic code.
- Integration with external vendors SHALL require a change record and business review before going live, with results documented for future audit and compliance needs.
- Ongoing review of integration impact on service stability, privacy, compliance, and user experience SHALL be conducted regularly as the todoApp evolves.

## Summary
TodoApp will operate as a fully functional, self-contained todo management system for its minimum viable product release. The only supported external integration at launch—if enabled—will be for email notification related to critical user-initiated workflows. All other integrations are considered future enhancements and must follow the specified business principles for modularity, security, user privacy, documentation, and auditable governance. The service is engineered for business agility and compliance, never compromising core functionality or user control regardless of integration status.

models.name: todo_app_users
models.description:
Registered user accounts for managing personal todo items.

This model stores unique member identities for end users of the Todo application. Each record captures essential account details required for secure authentication, session management, and privacy enforcement per user. All registered users are uniquely identified by email, with password hashing for credential security. Users may create, update, complete, and delete their own todos, with strict enforcement that no user may access or modify another account's todos. The table supports account recovery and compliance with data erasure policies. Admin accounts are managed separately to preserve strong privilege separation.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address for authentication and account notifications. Enforced as unique across all users.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed representation of the user's password. Plaintext values are never stored or processed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for the last update to the user's account data.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for GDPR/account deletion and recovery workflows.

models.name: todo_app_user_sessions
models.description:
Session records for authenticated user activity tracking.

This subsidiary table logs all active and historical login sessions for each user, enabling secure authentication state management, audit trails, and session expiry enforcement. It captures the context of each login, including IP, originating URL, and referrer information, as well as lifecycle timestamps. Each session references its owner user and is never shared across users. Sessions may expire naturally or be terminated for security reasons. The table enforces auditability and supports forensic analysis during security events or account changes.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: References the unique user who owns this session. {@link todo_app_users.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the application entry point for the session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL initiating sign-in session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp. Set when the session naturally concludes or is terminated.

models.name: todo_app_admins
models.description:
System administrator accounts with global oversight authority.

This model manages all privileged identities authorized to oversee, support, and manage the entire Todo application, including all user and todo records. Admin accounts are strictly segregated from regular user accounts to preserve least-privilege policy and support regulatory compliance. Each admin is identified by a unique email, with a securely hashed password for exclusive authentication. Deletion and modification actions by admins are audited, and extended account management privileges are restricted to this class. Suitable for future extension to audit or multi-role administration.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address for administrator authentication. Must be unique across all admins.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password credential for administrator authentication. Plaintext passwords are never stored.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp for the administrator account.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for the administrator record.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for compliance or admin removal events.

models.name: todo_app_admin_sessions
models.description:
Session tracking for administrator authentication events.

This model logs all authentication sessions for administrators only, capturing the connection context and session lifecycle details for compliance and audit purposes. Each session is strictly tied to a unique admin account and includes IP, href, referrer, and timestamps. The subsidiary stance enforces that sessions are managed through admin workflows, and each login event is auditable for security reviews. No overlap occurs with user session management, preserving strong privilege boundaries. Supports account lockout, session expiry, and future multifactor authentication enhancements.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: References the unique administrator who owns this session. {@link todo_app_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the administrator session was created.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Entry URL for admin session sign-in.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that originated the admin session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session initiation timestamp.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp marking the end or expiry of the administrator's session.

models.name: todo_app_todos
models.description:
Primary business entity for all todo tasks in the application.

Represents an individual todo item uniquely owned by a single user ({@link todo_app_users}). Each todo captures the required title, optional description, and full set of business lifecycle states (active, completed, deleted) via the status field and corresponding timestamps. Enforces unique todo titles among a user's active items, supports optional due date, and maintains full audit fields for creation, modification, completion, and soft deletion. Todos are strictly private and accessible only to the user and system administrators; all visibility and permissions are managed at the application layer. All state transitions (completion, deletion, recovery) are reflected in status and timestamp columns; permanent erasure after retention period is carried out by application logic. The model allows efficient queries on ownership, state, and business constraints, and is ready for enterprise-scale extensions (archiving, snapshot/audit, future features).

foreignFields.name: todo_app_user_id
foreignFields.description: Owner of this todo. References the primary key in the users table. {@link todo_app_users.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Required, user-defined name of todo item. Must be unique among active todos for the same user. Maximum 100 characters.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional, user-supplied description of the todo. Maximum 1000 characters. May be null if the user chooses not to enter details.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current business status of the todo. One of: 'active', 'completed', 'deleted'. Transitions controlled by user actions and business rules.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Optional due date for task completion. Null if no due date is set. Must be a future date at the time of entry.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of todo creation (UTC, immutable). Set once at row insertion.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update to title, description, due date, or other editable fields. Updated automatically on modification.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when todo was marked as completed. Only set when status='completed'; otherwise null.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when todo was deleted (soft delete). Set when status transitions to 'deleted', otherwise null. Used for retention/erasure rules.

### `todo_app_users`

Registered user accounts for managing personal todo items.

This model stores unique member identities for end users of the Todo
application. Each record captures essential account details required for
secure authentication, session management, and privacy enforcement per
user. All registered users are uniquely identified by email, with
password hashing for credential security. Users may create, update,
complete, and delete their own todos, with strict enforcement that no
user may access or modify another account's todos. The table supports
account recovery and compliance with data erasure policies. Admin
accounts are managed separately to preserve strong privilege separation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Unique email address for authentication and account notifications.
  > Enforced as unique across all users.
- `password_hash`
  > Securely hashed representation of the user's password. Plaintext values
  > are never stored or processed.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the user account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for the last update to the user's account data.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp for GDPR/account deletion and recovery workflows.

### `todo_app_user_sessions`

Session records for authenticated user activity tracking.

This subsidiary table logs all active and historical login sessions for
each user, enabling secure authentication state management, audit trails,
and session expiry enforcement. It captures the context of each login,
including IP, originating URL, and referrer information, as well as
lifecycle timestamps. Each session references its owner user and is never
shared across users. Sessions may expire naturally or be terminated for
security reasons. The table enforces auditability and supports forensic
analysis during security events or account changes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_id`
  > References the unique user who owns this session. {@link
  > todo_app_users.id}.
- `ip`: IP address from which the session was initiated.
- `href`: URL of the application entry point for the session.
- `referrer`: Referrer URL initiating sign-in session.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the session was created.
- `expired_at`
  > Session expiration timestamp. Set when the session naturally concludes or
  > is terminated.

### `todo_app_admins`

System administrator accounts with global oversight authority.

This model manages all privileged identities authorized to oversee,
support, and manage the entire Todo application, including all user and
todo records. Admin accounts are strictly segregated from regular user
accounts to preserve least-privilege policy and support regulatory
compliance. Each admin is identified by a unique email, with a securely
hashed password for exclusive authentication. Deletion and modification
actions by admins are audited, and extended account management privileges
are restricted to this class. Suitable for future extension to audit or
multi-role administration.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Unique email address for administrator authentication. Must be unique
  > across all admins.
- `password_hash`
  > Hashed password credential for administrator authentication. Plaintext
  > passwords are never stored.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for the administrator account.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for the administrator record.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp for compliance or admin removal events.

### `todo_app_admin_sessions`

Session tracking for administrator authentication events.

This model logs all authentication sessions for administrators only,
capturing the connection context and session lifecycle details for
compliance and audit purposes. Each session is strictly tied to a unique
admin account and includes IP, href, referrer, and timestamps. The
subsidiary stance enforces that sessions are managed through admin
workflows, and each login event is auditable for security reviews. No
overlap occurs with user session management, preserving strong privilege
boundaries. Supports account lockout, session expiry, and future
multifactor authentication enhancements.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `admin_id`
  > References the unique administrator who owns this session. {@link
  > todo_app_admins.id}.
- `ip`: IP address from which the administrator session was created.
- `href`: Entry URL for admin session sign-in.
- `referrer`: Referrer URL that originated the admin session.
- `created_at`: Session initiation timestamp.
- `expired_at`: Timestamp marking the end or expiry of the administrator's session.

### `todo_app_todos`

Primary business entity for all todo tasks in the application.

Represents an individual todo item uniquely owned by a single user
([todo_app_users](#todo_app_users)). Each todo captures the required title, optional
description, and full set of business lifecycle states (active,
completed, deleted) via the status field and corresponding timestamps.
Enforces unique todo titles among a user's active items, supports
optional due date, and maintains full audit fields for creation,
modification, completion, and soft deletion. Todos are strictly private
and accessible only to the user and system administrators; all visibility
and permissions are managed at the application layer. All state
transitions (completion, deletion, recovery) are reflected in status and
timestamp columns; permanent erasure after retention period is carried
out by application logic. The model allows efficient queries on
ownership, state, and business constraints, and is ready for
enterprise-scale extensions (archiving, snapshot/audit, future features).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_user_id`
  > Owner of this todo. References the primary key in the users table. {@link
  > todo_app_users.id}.
- `title`
  > Required, user-defined name of todo item. Must be unique among active
  > todos for the same user. Maximum 100 characters.
- `description`
  > Optional, user-supplied description of the todo. Maximum 1000 characters.
  > May be null if the user chooses not to enter details.
- `status`
  > Current business status of the todo. One of: 'active', 'completed',
  > 'deleted'. Transitions controlled by user actions and business rules.
- `due_date`
  > Optional due date for task completion. Null if no due date is set. Must
  > be a future date at the time of entry.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of todo creation (UTC, immutable). Set once at row insertion.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of last update to title, description, due date, or other
  > editable fields. Updated automatically on modification.
- `completed_at`
  > Timestamp when todo was marked as completed. Only set when
  > status='completed'; otherwise null.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when todo was deleted (soft delete). Set when status
  > transitions to 'deleted', otherwise null. Used for retention/erasure
  > rules.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new todo item for the authenticated user in the todo_app_todos table. It requires the todo title and allows providing an optional description and due date. The creation sets the todo as 'active' by default, assigns it to the requesting user based on authentication context, and automatically populates audit fields (created_at and updated_at). The operation enforces uniqueness of the todo title for the user's active todos, supports maximum length constraints (title: 100, description: 1000), and validates that the due date (if supplied) must be a valid future datetime. All todos are user-private and are not accessible to other users. On success, the detailed todo object is returned, reflecting complete server-calculated status fields and timestamps. The operation is strictly for authenticated users (not admins), and only the owner may create their own todos.
operations.description:
Create a new todo item owned by the currently authenticated user.

This endpoint enables users to add personal todo items with required title, optional description, and optional due date. It ensures that no other active todo for the same user has the same title, providing clear error feedback if this constraint is violated.

The status of the new todo is set to 'active'. The server-side automatically fills in the creation and update timestamps. If a due_date is provided, it must meet validation criteria for being in the future.

Security is enforced by limiting access to authenticated users only, with enforcement at the controller and provider levels. Other users and administrators cannot create todos on someone else's behalf. This operation references the todo_app_todos Prisma schema and leverages the relationships and field constraints defined there.

On successful creation, the response returns the fully detailed todo object, including business-state and audit fields. Any errors in validation or uniqueness constraints are clearly reported through standardized error responses. Related operations include updating, marking complete, listing, and deleting todos.

It allows modification of the title (with uniqueness enforced among active todos), description, due date, and optionally status to mark the todo complete or deleted (soft delete) as per business lifecycle. Modification is only permitted if the todo has not been permanently erased. The operation ensures all string length, timestamp, and enum constraints from the Prisma schema are enforced. Ownership validation guarantees that users can only modify their own todos, and administrators are forbidden from using this endpoint. All changes result in appropriate updating of modification and completion timestamps as defined in schema business rules. Upon success, the full, detailed todo object is returned including all state and audit fields reflecting the update.

Update mutable fields of an existing todo item owned by the authenticated user.

This endpoint supports changes to the title, description, due date, and status of the todo. Title changes are subject to uniqueness checks among the user's non-deleted todos. If status is set to 'completed' or 'deleted', the relevant business rule triggers (such as updating completed_at or deleted_at) are handled internally.

Access is strictly limited to the owner of the todo; administrators and non-owners are forbidden from using this endpoint. All updates result in refresh of the updated_at field. The operation draws all business logic and validation from the todo_app_todos Prisma schema, using only allowed transitions and field constraints.

If the todo is successfully updated, the complete todo object (with refreshed audit fields and current status) is returned. If the operation fails due to permission, uniqueness, or validation errors, standardized error responses are returned to the client. Related endpoints include creation, listing, marking complete, and deleting todos.

The deletion targets a single todo, identified uniquely by its database UUID, and removes it completely from storage regardless of its prior status. The operation bypasses the standard soft deletion (status='deleted' and deleted_at set) and ensures the todo record is no longer present after execution. Ownership is validated to restrict erasure to the user who owns the todo or system administrators. Audit and business logic must track this action due to irreversible consequence; retention and regulatory policies should be enforced prior to invocation. This operation uses the 'id' (UUID) primary key of the todo_app_todos model.
operations.description:
Permanently erase a single todo item from the application database.

This operation allows an authenticated user (the owner of the todo item) or a privileged administrator to permanently delete a specific todo. Once executed, the record is removed from the todo_app_todos table, bypassing soft deletion and retention tracking. The API validates both user ownership and proper authorization before proceeding; users may only erase their own todos while administrators have global authority.

Deletion is irreversible and is intended for cases such as compliance-driven purging or user-requested permanent erasure. All business and regulatory checks (such as legal retention periods or audit requirements) must be completed before calling this endpoint. Related operations include soft-deletion (by updating status), list retrieval for user's todos, and administrator endpoint for bulk erasure.

Path parameter validation ensures only valid UUID values are accepted; appropriate error responses must be returned for invalid, non-existent, or unauthorized requests.

Typical use-cases include marking several todos as completed, updating due dates in batch, or soft-deleting a group of items. The operation accepts an array of todo UUIDs and an update payload that describes the desired change (e.g., status, due_date, title). It validates ownership for all todos, ensuring only the authenticated user's items are modified unless performed by an administrator. The business logic enforces database constraints on title uniqueness (within the user's active todos), valid status transitions, and timestamp updates according to the specified changes. Efficient for user-driven mass modifications and compliant with audit/event tracking requirements. This operation does not support permanent deletion (hard erase); use the individual erase endpoint or admin tools for permanent purging.
operations.description:
Modify multiple todo items in a single request for advanced user convenience and workflow optimization.

This operation lets users perform actions (such as batch completion, updating descriptions, or soft-deletion) on multiple todos at once, identified by their unique UUIDs. The request body provides a list of todo IDs and an update object specifying the fields to apply to all selected todos. Security checks ensure each todo belongs to the requesting user or that administrative permissions are in effect. Title uniqueness among active todos is enforced per business rules; conflicts should generate errors for affected items without breaking the batch.

The operation is optimized for efficiency and integrates audit trail recording for all changes. Use-case examples include 'complete all overdue tasks' or 'assign due date to selected todos'. Permanent deletion is not supported by this endpoint and must be done individually via the erase endpoint or by system administrators.

ITodoAppUser.description:
Detailed user account information for registered Todo App users.

Represents all non-sensitive, non-authentication fields from the todo_app_users table. Used for administrative inspection and user self-management, excluding password hash details for privacy and security.

Enables account review, account update and deletion operations. Supports privacy compliance with soft deletion tracking via deleted_at.

id.description: Unique identifier of the user (Primary Key).

email.description: Unique email address for authentication and account notifications. Enforced as unique across all users.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last modification of the user's account data.

oneOf.description: Soft delete timestamp for GDPR/account deletion and recovery workflows.
Null if the account is active and not deleted.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp or null if account is active.

email.description:
Unique email address of the registering user.

Used as the primary identifier for login and notification. Must comply with unique constraint and email formatting rules. Provided by the client during registration.

password.description:
Plain text password provided by the user at registration.

This property is required only for join (self-signup) and login operations. The value is securely hashed server-side before being stored as password_hash in the database. Must meet minimum length and business password policy for security. Plain text password is never stored or returned in any response.

href.description:
Connection URL (current page URL) where registration is submitted from.

Required for session context, security auditing, and potential fraud detection. Must be a valid URI. Captured from the user's browser upon registration.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page) for additional session tracking and security context.

Required for session and fraud analysis. Can be empty string if direct access, otherwise should be the actual referrer.

ip.description:
Optional client IP address for session and security context.

Supplied if available (client or fronting proxy can provide), otherwise the backend will infer. Used for security auditing and fraud prevention. Accepts both IPv4 and IPv6 string formats, or null if unavailable.

ITodoAppUser.IJoin.description:
Information required to register a new user account on the todo application.

Must include a unique email and password that meet system requirements. Security: the password is stored as a secure hash (password_hash on the database) and never logged or returned in plaintext. Registration also captures session context fields (href, referrer, and optionally ip) for auditability and security tracking. Ensures robust user authentication, fraud detection, and compliance with data protection policies.

ITodoAppUser.ILogin.description:
Login request for regular member of the todo_app_users table.

This schema is used to accept user credentials during the login process for end users of the Todo application. The user must supply a registered email and the plain text password (which is validated by hashing and comparing with the password_hash field in the database).

This login request never exposes or requires password hashes. Session context for audit/tracking is handled in subsidiary tables, not in this DTO. This DTO is only for supplying credentials.

email.description: Registered email address of the user for authentication. Must be unique across all user accounts.

password.description: User's plain text password for authentication. This value is validated against the password_hash in the database and is never stored or logged in plain text.

id.description: Unique identifier (id field of todo_app_users) for the authenticated user. Used for reference in subsequent operations and session validation.

email.description: Authenticated user's email address, sourced from todo_app_users. Used for UI display and audit tracking.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last modification of the user's account data.

oneOf.description: Soft delete timestamp for GDPR/account deletion and recovery workflows.
Null if the account is active and not deleted.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp or null if account is active.

ITodoAppUser.IAuthorized.description:
Represents authenticated user session information and issued tokens.

Returned after successful registration (join), login, or refresh actions for todo_app_users. This entity provides user identity and active session information, along with JWT tokens required for ongoing authentication. The token property references the authorization token structure, which embeds access and refresh tokens. Sensitive authentication material (password) is never returned.

ITodoAppUser.IRefresh.description:
Refresh request for the todo_app_users authentication lifecycle.

This DTO allows a user to supply their previously issued refresh token to obtain new JWT session tokens. The supplied token is validated and not stored after inspection. Used in the persistent authentication pattern for member users.

Refresh request does not require or reference password or personal user details; it is strictly token-centric. Only valid refresh tokens from previous successful login or join are accepted, in accordance with the authentication policies established in the service requirements.

refresh_token.description: Previously issued refresh token for the user session. Must be provided exactly as issued by previous authentication (login or join). Used to validate the user's continued access without password reentry.

ITodoAppAdmin.IJoin.description:
Request DTO for onboarding (registering) a new administrator in the Todo application.

Requires a unique email address and a plain password, both validated to meet business and schema constraints. Upon join, a new administrator account is created in the todo_app_admins table, and a new admin session is initiated.

Session context fields (href and referrer) are required—these record the connection URL and referrer for auditing and compliance. The IP address is optionally accepted and will be set from request context if omitted. Security policies enforce that password must be sent as plain text so backend can hash it securely, regardless of the corresponding database column name. This schema is strictly for administrative self-join; admin-created users use a different DTO.

email.description: Administrator's unique email address used for authentication. Must not duplicate any existing admin email.

password.description: Administrator password in plain text for registration. Backend securely hashes this before storing in password_hash. Strong policy: not stored or logged in plaintext. Must satisfy all application password rules.

oneOf.description: Optional client IP address for session tracking (IPv4 or IPv6). Usually set automatically by backend, but explicitly accepted for compliance or SSR contexts.
Optional client IP address for session tracking (IPv4 or IPv6). Usually set automatically by backend, but explicitly accepted for compliance or SSR contexts.
Explicitly null IP address, forcing backend to use detected client IP.

ip.description: IP address from which the administrator session is created. Must be valid IPv4 or IPv6. Optional—if omitted, backend uses connection context.

href.description: Required connection URL (current page URL) for session auditing. Used to link this session with the admin's point of registration. Must be a well-formed absolute URL.

referrer.description: Required referrer URL (page that initiated admin registration). Used for compliance and session provenance tracking. Must be a well-formed absolute URL.

ITodoAppAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Response DTO for authorized administrator sessions after join, login, or refresh operations.

Provides the administrator's UUID, email, and details necessary for authenticated application operation. Includes an authorization token structure containing issued JWT access and refresh tokens tied to this admin session. The session's creation timestamp confirms the moment of authorization and may be used for downstream compliance checks. Password hashes and sensitive credential information are strictly omitted by security policy.

This DTO enables all privileged operations for the authenticated admin. The session model is strictly for admin (not regular user) authentication contexts. Use only for endpoints which securely issue or renew admin credentials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the administrator account. Corresponds to todo_app_admins.id.

email.description: Administrator's unique email address as returned from the system. Corresponds to todo_app_admins.email.

password_hash.description:
The securely hashed password credential for administrator authentication.

Plaintext passwords are never stored. This value represents the output of a secure, salted password hasher (such as bcrypt or Argon2) and is used exclusively for credential verification. Sensitive: never expose to non-admin users.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp for the administrator record. Corresponds to todo_app_admins.created_at.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp for this administrator. Corresponds to todo_app_admins.updated_at.

deleted_at.description:
Soft delete timestamp for compliance or admin removal events.

Set to a date-time value when the administrator account is soft deleted for regulatory compliance, security, or deactivation purposes. Null if the account is active.

session.description: Summary of the session that was established for this admin authentication event, as tracked in todo_app_admin_sessions.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the administrator session record. Serves as the primary key for session tracking in the database. Automatically generated as a UUID for every new session.

This value is essential for auditing, reconciliation, and regulatory reporting regarding privileged access events by any administrator.

admin_id.description:
References the administrator who owns this session. Directly mapped to "admin_id" in the database, which references the corresponding admin account's primary key in todo_app_admins.

This linkage establishes authority and privilege hierarchy for session-based auditing and supports regulatory and segregation-of-duties reviews.

ip.description:
IP address from which the administrator session was created. Used for auditing, fraud detection, risk scoring, and tracking security breaches.

Captures the network origin for each administrator login. Required by compliance policies to enable tracking and detection of suspicious access patterns.

href.description:
Entry URL for the admin session sign-in. Captures the page/location from which privileged authentication was initiated.

This supports traceability for audit investigations, showing the workflow or page where a session started.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that originated the admin session event. Indicates the user journey before privileged login occurred.

Used during audits to determine whether sessions originated from expected or unexpected sources, and supports detailed session provenance.

created_at.description:
Session initiation timestamp (ISO 8601 date-time). Indicates when this privileged admin session started.

Used for compliance timing reconciliation, session lifecycle tracking, and long-term audit history.

ITodoAppAdminSession.ISummary.description:
Summary information for a privileged administrator session event in the Todo application backend.

This schema is designed primarily for audit, compliance, and privileged access monitoring. It represents a subsidiary model strictly tied to administrator authentication and is never exposed to regular user operations. Each session instance records detailed context (administrator, network, and origination data) for security posture enforcement, compliance reporting, and intrusion analysis.

The 'subsidiary' stance of this entity is enforced throughout the system, preventing overlap with regular user session management and strengthening least-privilege boundaries. Session lifecycle management ensures proper account lockout, future multifactor extensions, and a complete forensic audit trail.

email.description:
Administrator email address used for authentication. Must be unique among all admin accounts.

Validated against RFC 5322 email format and checked against the unique index on todo_app_admins.email. Serves as the primary credential for admin login and privilege escalation tracking. Only valid accounts may proceed through authentication, and access is denied for soft-deleted (deleted_at not null) records.

password.description:
Plaintext password for privileged admin login. Must comply with the configured password policy for length, complexity, and rotation (minimum 8 characters by system default).

Never persisted in the backend. Used for secure cryptographic comparison against the password_hash in todo_app_admins. Failed comparisons or excessive failed attempts result in account lockout or potential security alerts/monitoring as defined by audit/compliance policies.

oneOf.description: IPv4 format IP address from which the login is being attempted. Used for audit context, regional monitoring, and breach detection.
IPv6 format IP address for login context.

No IP provided. Backend automatically extracts the network origin during request processing if missing.

Allowing null enables robust fallback, and all logins are still fully traceable for regulatory purposes even without explicit client IP. Strategic in situations where session origination context must be inferred from reverse proxies or intermediate layers.

ip.description:
IP address for session context. Optionally provided by the client, but if absent or null, will be reliably extracted server-side for all administrative login attempts.

Captures full network context for audit, risk mitigation, and fraud detection. Compliance policy requires every admin login event to be traceable to a network origin.

href.description:
Full URL of the sign-in page or client location when initiating privileged administrator login.

Essential for supporting traceable and auditable session context, as required by security and compliance audits. Aids investigations by tracking which workflow or resource led to authentication. Required for every privileged login attempt.

referrer.description:
The referrer URL that led to the administrator login page or workflow. Captured as part of session context for audit and compliance investigations.

Required for each admin login to provide additional provenance for security monitoring.

ITodoAppAdmin.ILogin.description:
Credentials for privileged administrator login to the Todo application backend.

This DTO captures all necessary details to establish a compliant audit trail for administrator authentication, including password policy enforcement and IP origination context.

The security posture enforced by this model strictly prevents unauthorized access and enables full session tracking for compliance with regulatory and audit standards. Designed for exclusive admin access and not exposed to regular user authentication, this schema embodies the least-privilege principle throughout the backend infrastructure.

refresh_token.description:
The opaque JWT refresh token for an admin session.

This token is required to renew access and refresh tokens for persistent administrator sessions. It must be an active, valid refresh token associated with a previous successful sign-in and session context.

ITodoAppAdmin.IRefresh.description:
Payload for administrative session refresh operation.

This DTO supplies the refresh token required for re-issuing JWT credentials to maintain administrator session continuity. The supplied token is verified against todo_app_admin_sessions and todo_app_admins for validity, status, and expiry enforcement. Used for session rotation/continuation in stateless admin workflows.

ITodoAppUser.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for admin-driven user queries.

Allows admins to page, filter, and search users by fields such as email, status, and registration timestamps. Excludes sensitive authentication data. Used as the request body for the admin user list/search operation.

page.description: Page number for pagination, starting at 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of users to return per page (default: 20, max: 100).

search.description: A partial email address or filter text for quick user search (applies partial match to email field).

oneOf.description: Account status filter: 'active' excludes deleted users, 'deleted' returns only soft-deleted accounts.
Account status filter: 'active' excludes deleted users, 'deleted' returns only soft-deleted accounts.

status.description: Account status filter: 'active' excludes deleted users, 'deleted' returns only soft-deleted accounts.

oneOf.description: Which user field to sort the results by (email, created_at, or updated_at).
Which user field to sort the results by (email, created_at, or updated_at).
Which user field to sort the results by (email, created_at, or updated_at).

sort_by.description: Which user field to sort the results by (email, created_at, or updated_at).

oneOf.description: Sort direction for user list.
Sort direction for user list.

ITodoAppUser.ISummary.description:
Summary view for registered user accounts in the Todo application.

Provides essential identity properties for a user, suitable for display in lists or embedding in related entities requiring user context.

This type excludes sensitive authentication fields (password_hash) and system fields only relevant for administration or auditing. Intended for client display, cross-entity embedding, and authorization context references.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user, assigned upon account creation.

email.description:
User's registered email address, used for authentication and communication.

This field is globally unique across all user accounts, ensuring reliable user identification.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last changes made to the user account (ISO 8601).

email.description: The user's unique email address for authentication and notifications. This must not conflict with another registered account, and must adhere to standard email format validation per RFC 5322. Changes must trigger system-side uniqueness checks and security auditing.

password.description: The new plain text password for the user account. This must meet all password complexity and minimum length requirements as defined in current business policy. This field is only accepted when a password change is requested; it must be securely hashed by the server before storage. Backend will enforce strict policies and never expose hashed representation to clients.

ITodoAppUser.IUpdate.description: DTO for updating current user's account in todo_app_users. Only optional fields are permitted: email or password. All updates are audited and subject to system validation. If both omitted, no-op. Ownership is immutable by design and may not be changed.

page.description: The page number for pagination (1-based). Used for paginated queries of user session records for administration or audit.

limit.description: The maximum number of session records per page, used for pagination. Must not exceed system maximum (default: 20, max: 100).

oneOf.description: Field to sort sessions by (created_at or expired_at). Controls display order for query results.
Field to sort sessions by (created_at or expired_at). Controls display order for query results.

sort.description: Field to sort sessions by (created_at or expired_at). Controls display order for query results.

oneOf.description: Sort order: ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Default is descending.
Sort order: ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Default is descending.

order.description: Sort order: ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Default is descending.

ip.description: Optional filter for session IP address. Restricts results to session records matching the given IP.

referrer.description: Optional filter for referrer URL of session initiation. Used to search sessions by source.

created_from.description: Start time filter for session creation timestamp. Restricts results to sessions created after this datetime.

created_to.description: End time filter for session creation timestamp. Restricts results to sessions created before this datetime.

expired.description: Optional filter to select expired or active sessions only. True = only expired; false = only active; omit or null = all.

ITodoAppUserSession.IRequest.description: Filtering and pagination parameters for admin session audit on a specific user's todo_app_user_sessions records. All fields are optional; combining filters further restricts results.

id.description:
Primary key identifier for the user session record.

This value uniquely identifies a single authentication session for a user of the Todo application. The session ID is generated at the time of authentication and is required for referencing, lookup, and audit purposes.

Linked to the todo_app_user_sessions table's `id` column.

user_id.description:
Unique identifier of the user owning this session.

This field references the `id` column in the todo_app_users table. It establishes the ownership relationship for this session, ensuring the session cannot be reassigned to different users.

ip.description:
IP address where the authentication session was established.

This value records the origin point of the user's login session, supporting audit trails, security events, geo-fencing, and session context analysis. This is required for every session and may be logged in both IPv4 and IPv6 format.

href.description:
The URL of the application entry point at the start of the session.

This value captures the context of the user's first connection for auditing, UI analytics, or support troubleshooting. Required on every session record for full session lifecycle traceability.

referrer.description:
The referring URL that initiated user authentication.

Records the navigation source leading to login; enables analysis of application flows and possible risk vectors. Required for all session records.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the login session was established.

This field follows ISO 8601 date-time format and is automatically generated by the system at session creation. Required for audit trail completeness and time-based session management.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session naturally expired or was otherwise terminated.

This field is set when the session has ended, either from user action, logout, or security policy enforcement. Use null for active (not yet expired) sessions. ISO 8601 datetime format required; field is nullable for active sessions.

ITodoAppUserSession.description:
Session record entity for tracking user authentication events and session lifecycle in the Todo List application.

Represents an individual session instance corresponding to a user's authenticated connection. Contains metadata required for auditing access, tracing user activity, and enforcing session security policies. Each session record links to a single user by `user_id`, with detailed session context (IP address, entry point URL, referrer, timestamps).

Session records are primarily used by admins for security investigations and regulatory compliance analysis. Records may be referenced in filtering or auditing scenarios.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results (1-based).

Controls pagination cursor for admin list queries. Minimum value is 1; typical usage is in conjunction with `limit` and `order_by`.

limit.description:
Maximum number of admin records to include in the result set per page.

This value limits the size of paginated results for efficient UI rendering and API bandwidth. Minimum value is 1; maximum is 100.

email.description:
Optional email filter (exact match or partial).

This parameter enables searching for admin records by email, supporting both partial and complete matches depending on the implementation context. Used to filter listing for audit or role review workflows.

created_at.description:
Optional filter for records created at or after this timestamp (ISO 8601 date-time format).

The value restricts results to administrator records created on or after the given date. Enables time-based audit reviews, system usage analysis, and regulatory compliance.

oneOf.description:
The field to use for sorting returned admin records ("created_at" or "email").

This restricts sorting to allowed fields for admin directory review/listing. Required if ordering is specified.

The field to use for sorting returned admin records ("created_at" or "email").

This restricts sorting to allowed fields for admin directory review/listing. Required if ordering is specified.

order_by.description:
The field to use for sorting returned admin records ("created_at" or "email").

This restricts sorting to allowed fields for admin directory review/listing. Required if ordering is specified.

oneOf.description:
The sort direction for the `order_by` field (ascending or descending).

Accepted values are "asc" for ascending, "desc" for descending. Controls display order for admin audit screens or exports.

The sort direction for the `order_by` field (ascending or descending).

Accepted values are "asc" for ascending, "desc" for descending. Controls display order for admin audit screens or exports.

sort.description:
The sort direction for the `order_by` field (ascending or descending).

Accepted values are "asc" for ascending, "desc" for descending. Controls display order for admin audit screens or exports.

ITodoAppAdmin.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for advanced filtering, pagination, and sorting of administrator accounts in the Todo List admin portal.

Enables privileged actors to list, search, and audit administrator records. All parameters are optional except where API requires pagination/sorting. Designed for compliance, role audit, and administrative management operations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the administrator account. This is the primary key and used to uniquely reference each admin across the system.

email.description: Unique email address for administrator authentication. Used as the primary credential for admin logins and must be unique across all administrators.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp for the administrator account. Indicates when the administrator account was first registered in the system.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp for the administrator record. Updated whenever administrator details are modified.

ITodoAppAdmin.ISummary.description:
Summary information for a Todo application system administrator.

This schema provides the essential details for displaying administrators in administrative lists or referencing them in relation to session or audit records. Only public non-sensitive fields are included, omitting authentication credentials and soft-deleted states. Suitable for summary displays and context links.

id.description:
Unique identifier (UUID) for the administrator account.

Serves as the primary key in the todo_app_admins table and is globally unique across all administrator accounts.
Used for identifying, retrieving, and managing specific administrator records throughout the system.

email.description:
Unique email address for administrator authentication.

Must be unique across all admins. Used as the login credential and for administrative communication, security notifications, and account recovery workflows.

password_hash.description:
The securely hashed password credential for administrator authentication.

Plaintext passwords are never stored. This value represents the output of a secure, salted password hasher (such as bcrypt or Argon2) and is used exclusively for credential verification. Sensitive: never expose to non-admin users.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp for the administrator account.

Indicates when the administrator account was originally created. Used for auditing and lifecycle management.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp for the administrator record.

Tracks the time of the most recent update to the administrator's profile, credentials, or account settings. Essential for compliance, auditing, and activity tracking.

deleted_at.description:
Soft delete timestamp for compliance or admin removal events.

Set to a date-time value when the administrator account is soft deleted for regulatory compliance, security, or deactivation purposes. Null if the account is active.

ITodoAppAdmin.description:
Administrator account entity for the Todo application.

Represents privileged system accounts authorized to oversee, support, and manage the entire Todo application. Admin accounts possess elevated permissions, are strictly segregated from regular user accounts, and are subject to auditing and compliance requirements.

All sensitive credential information (such as password_hash) is included here only for administrative and audit workflows—never expose this information to non-privileged contexts. Account lifecycle metadata such as creation and update timestamps, as well as soft deletion status, are also present for system management and regulatory oversight.

email.description: The new administrator email (must remain unique). Used for authentication and notifications. Changing this value requires uniqueness validation and may trigger account security alerts.

password_hash.description: The new securely hashed password credential if being rotated/reset. Should represent a secure salted hash generated from the administrator's new password. Used only for credential updates; omit if not changing password.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for when the administrator's record was last modified. Set automatically when a relevant property is changed. Ensures update operation is auditable.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete or restore flag for the administrator account. Set to a date-time value to deactivate (soft delete) the admin, or to null to restore/reactivate. Used for compliance and access management. Omit or set to null if not changing the deletion status.

ITodoAppAdmin.IUpdate.description:
DTO schema for updating administrator account records in the Todo application.

Allows privileged users to update administrator credentials (email, password) and soft delete status for compliance and security workflows. Excludes immutable fields such as id and created_at. All properties are optional to support partial updates, and sensitive fields require appropriate security and validation handling on change.

ITodoAppAdminSession.IRequest.description:
Query and filter options for retrieving administrator session records from the todo_app_admin_sessions table.

Supports pagination, advanced search, sorting, and field-based filtering to aid privileged administrative audit, compliance reporting, and session review. All query parameters apply to sessions associated with a specific admin. Typical filter fields include creation and expiry timestamps, IP address, referrer, and entry URL for session context tracking. Pagination, sorting, and search fields are required for scalable data management.

Sessions are subsidiary records, always accessed under the context of a parent admin actor, and return summary information for each session matching the search criteria.

page.description: Page number for results pagination. Must be 1 or higher.

limit.description: Maximum number of session records per page. Must be between 1 and 100.

search.description: General search keyword to match relevant session metadata such as IP, referrer, or href. Used for free-text search filtering.

oneOf.description: Field to sort results by. Can be either session creation time ('created_at') or expiry ('expired_at').
Field to sort results by. Can be either session creation time ('created_at') or expiry ('expired_at').

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by. Can be either session creation time ('created_at') or expiry ('expired_at').

oneOf.description: Sort direction for result ordering. Ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc').
Sort direction for result ordering. Ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc').

sort_order.description: Sort direction for result ordering. Ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc').

ip.description: Filter sessions by client IP address used at login.

href.description: Filter sessions by entry URL at session initiation.

referrer.description: Filter sessions by referrer URL present when session was created.

created_from.description: Filter for sessions created after this timestamp (inclusive). ISO 8601 datetime.

created_to.description: Filter for sessions created before this timestamp (inclusive). ISO 8601 datetime.

expired_from.description: Filter for sessions expired after this timestamp (inclusive). ISO 8601 datetime.

expired_to.description: Filter for sessions expired before this timestamp (inclusive). ISO 8601 datetime.

ITodoAppAdminSession.description:
Administrator authentication/session record associated with a privileged admin account.

Captures session lifecycle properties for administrator sign-in events, including IP, entry URL, referrer, creation, (if ended) expiry timestamps, and the owning admin record. Each session is associated with a unique todo_app_admins account via the admin_id foreign key, and is auditable for security and compliance.

This schema is used in detailed session review, security audit, and privileged login tracking. Closely reflects the Prisma model fields for accurate data mapping and enforcement of business constraints.

id.description: Unique identifier for this admin session (Primary Key from todo_app_admin_sessions). Used for direct session retrieval and reference in administrative operations.

admin_id.description: References the unique administrator (todo_app_admins) who owns this session. The value is the UUID primary key and is used as a foreign key in the session record. Required for accurate relationship mapping.

admin.description: Denormalized summary information of the administrator account linked to this session. Provides convenient contextual display in responses, but 'admin_id' is the authoritative database key.

ip.description: IP address from which the administrator session was created, as captured at sign-in. Used for security audits and intrusion detection.

href.description: Entry URL for admin session sign-in, recording which page the login originated from.

referrer.description: Referrer URL that originated the administrator session. Accountability for session context and referral sources.

created_at.description: Session initiation timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC format.

expired_at.description: Timestamp marking session end or expiry. If null, the session is still active.

ITodoAppTodo.description:
Main business entity representing a single Todo item in the application. This object includes all primary fields, business-state, audit, and lifecycle metadata as defined in the todo_app_todos Prisma schema.

Each todo is uniquely identified by its id and strictly owned by one user (owner relationship modeled via foreign key to todo_app_users, see todo_app_user_id). The object contains the core business data (title, description, status, due_date), full audit fields (created_at, updated_at), and lifecycle markers (completed_at, deleted_at).

Todos are strictly private to users and never exposed to other end-users without appropriate permission. All field constraints, relationships, and validation rules are enforced as in the Prisma definition.

Relationship: Ownership is referenced via user identity from authentication context; the todo_app_user_id field establishes this link.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item (primary key). UUID assigned at creation and immutable.

title.description: User-defined name for the todo item. Required. Must be unique among a user's active todos. Maximum 100 characters as per Prisma schema.

oneOf.description: Optional user-supplied description for the todo task. Up to 1000 characters allowed. Can be null if omitted.

description.description: Optional user-supplied description for the todo task. Up to 1000 characters allowed. Can be null if omitted.

oneOf.description: Current business state of the todo. Enum: 'active', 'completed', 'deleted' (by Prisma schema). Controls allowed transitions and client UI.
Current business state of the todo. Enum: 'active', 'completed', 'deleted' (by Prisma schema). Controls allowed transitions and client UI.
Current business state of the todo. Enum: 'active', 'completed', 'deleted' (by Prisma schema). Controls allowed transitions and client UI.

status.description: Current business state of the todo. Enum: 'active', 'completed', 'deleted' (by Prisma schema). Controls allowed transitions and client UI.

oneOf.description: Optional due date for task completion. Must be a future date when set. Null when not specified.

due_date.description: Optional due date/time for the todo item. ISO 8601 (UTC), nullable.

created_at.description: Timestamp of creation (UTC, immutable). Set on insertion. Never changes.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last update to any editable field (title, description, due date, etc.). Updated automatically on modification.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the todo was marked as completed. Nullable: only set if status is 'completed', otherwise null.

completed_at.description: When set, the datetime the todo was completed. Null unless status is 'completed'.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the todo was deleted (soft delete). Set when status transitions to 'deleted', otherwise null. Used for retention/erasure rules.

deleted_at.description: Datetime when item was softly deleted by user. Null unless status = 'deleted'.

todo_app_user_id.description: UUID referencing the user who owns this todo item. Relationship to todo_app_users.id. Ownership is enforced by system logic. Not present in request bodies; included here for entity-level DTO for administrative/audit purposes.

ITodoAppTodo.IRequest.description:
Search and query logic for paginated retrieval of todo items. Used as the request body schema for endpoints allowing advanced filtering, searching, and sorting of todos (see /todoApp/user/todos PATCH operation).

Permits filtering by status, owner, date range, partial title or description, and supports pagination and sorting based on available fields. Null/shorthand properties meaning "no filter" or "default" are supported. All fields are optional; only provided filters/sorters are applied.

Intended for use by authenticated users and system administrators within search UI flows.

title.description: Filter todos by partial title (case-insensitive, substring match). Maximum 100 characters. Optional; if not provided, matches any title.

description.description: Filter todos by partial description (case-insensitive, substring match). Maximum 1000 characters. Optional.

oneOf.description: Filter by business status (enum: 'active', 'completed', 'deleted'). Optional; if not provided, returns todos of any status.
Filter by business status (enum: 'active', 'completed', 'deleted'). Optional; if not provided, returns todos of any status.
Filter by business status (enum: 'active', 'completed', 'deleted'). Optional; if not provided, returns todos of any status.

status.description: Filter by business status (enum: 'active', 'completed', 'deleted'). Optional; if not provided, returns todos of any status.

due_date_from.description: Filter: Only todos with due_date >= this value are included. ISO 8601 UTC datetime string. Optional.

due_date_to.description: Filter: Only todos with due_date <= this value are included. ISO 8601 UTC datetime string. Optional.

created_at_from.description: Filter: Only todos with created_at >= this value are included. ISO 8601 UTC datetime string. Optional.

created_at_to.description: Filter: Only todos with created_at <= this value are included. ISO 8601 UTC datetime string. Optional.

owner_user_id.description: For administrative search: filter todos to only those owned by the given user. UUID format. Optional; regular users must not set this. Required for admin global queries.

oneOf.description: Sort results by this field. Supported fields: 'title', 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'due_date', 'status'. Optional; defaults to descending created_at if not provided.
