ITodoAppTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for a single todo item in the todo_app_todos table.

Used in list views and as a reference in other DTOs to represent an individual todo item owned by a user. Provides identifying fields and current business state, enabling efficient display, filtering, and permission checks without exposing full task details.

This schema is optimized for performance and usability in bulk queries and UI components. Nullable fields communicate lifecycle event milestones (due, completed, deleted).

title.description: Required, user-defined name of the todo item. Must be unique among active todos for the same user. Maximum 100 characters. Cannot be empty or whitespace only.

oneOf.description: Optional, user-supplied description of the todo. Maximum 1000 characters. May be null if the user chooses not to enter details.
Indicates that the user has not provided a description.

description.description: Optional description for the todo task supplied by the user. Null if user did not provide one. Maximum 1000 characters.

oneOf.description: The due date/time by which the todo should be completed. If provided, must be a valid RFC 3339 timestamp string in the future at the time of creation.
No due date has been set for this task.

due_date.description: Optional due date for task completion. Must be a valid future datetime string when provided. Null if no due date is set.

ITodoAppTodo.ICreate.description:
Schema for creating a new todo item for the authenticated user. Represents a personal task to be tracked in the user's todo list.

Includes the required todo title and optional description and due date fields. The owning user is determined by authentication context, and cannot be provided client-side. The title must be unique among non-deleted todos for the user and is limited to 100 characters. Description may be omitted or set to null. If a due date is supplied, it must be a valid UTC datetime string in the future.

Audit fields and ownership are managed by the server. Status is initialized as 'active' on creation, with timestamps for creation and update set automatically. No system or authentication fields are supplied by the client.

ITodoAppTodo.IUpdate.description: The new fields to be applied to all affected todos in the bulk operation. All fields are optional; only provided keys will be updated.

title.description: Optional new title for the todo. Must be unique among the user's active todos. Maximum 100 characters.

oneOf.description: Optional new description for the todo. Maximum 1000 characters.

description.description: New description for the todo, or null to clear. Maximum 1000 characters.

oneOf.description: Optional new due date for the todo. Must be a valid future ISO 8601 date-time.

due_date.description: New due date for the todo or null to clear.

oneOf.description: New status for the todo. Must be one of: 'active', 'completed', or 'deleted'. Transitions must follow business state rules.
New status for the todo. Must be one of: 'active', 'completed', or 'deleted'. Transitions must follow business state rules.
New status for the todo. Must be one of: 'active', 'completed', or 'deleted'. Transitions must follow business state rules.

status.description: New status for the todo. Must be one of: 'active', 'completed', or 'deleted'. Transitions must follow business state rules.

ITodoAppTodo.IBulkUpdate.description:
Request payload for batch updating multiple todos in a single operation for advanced user productivity.

Enables updates to a selection of todos owned by the user. Accepts a list of todo UUIDs identifying the items to change along with an update object specifying the properties to modify (e.g., status, due_date, title). Ownership validation and business rules (including title uniqueness per user, valid lifecycle transitions, audit field updates, soft deletion semantics, and restriction of hard delete) are strictly enforced. Used in mass completion, batch editing, and similar workflow scenarios. Does not allow permanent erasure, which must be performed per-todo via erase endpoint or by admin.

items.description: UUID of the todo to be updated. Must reference a todo owned by the requesting user.

ids.description: List of todo IDs to update in the batch operation. Each must correspond to a todo the requester is permitted to modify.

update.description: Update object describing the fields to be applied to all specified todos. Represents a partial update with optional fields mirroring the allowed editable properties of a todo (title, description, due_date, status).

ITodoAppTodo.IBulkUpdateResult.description:
Response object representing the outcome of a batch todo update operation.

Details, for each requested todo, whether the specified change succeeded or failed (with error reasons). Ensures outcome transparency for user workflows and proper audit trail recording.

results.description: Result for each todo specified in the request. Each entry details the id, operation result, and error information if any.

ITodoAppTodo.IBulkUpdateResultItem.description:
Describes the outcome of a single todo processed by a bulk update request.

Used in the results array of the bulk update response, so every batch request can see which items succeeded or failed and why.

id.description: UUID of the todo item processed.

success.description: Indicates overall success (true) or failure (false) for this todo's update operation.

oneOf.description: If present, contains a business or validation error message explaining failure.

error.description: Populated if the update failed for this todo. Null on success.

ITodoAppUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a user session for activity auditing and context embedding.

Captures session metadata for an authenticated user, providing information for security auditing, history lists, or cross-entity context.

Sensitive authentication fields are excluded. Session is always referenced by its unique identifier and associated timestamps for lifecycle analysis.

id.description: Unique identifier for the session, assigned at creation.

user_id.description: Reference to the user who owns this session. Matches the user account's unique identifier.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was initiated.

href.description: URL of the application entry point where session authentication began.

referrer.description: Referrer URL from which the user initiated the authentication session.

created_at.description: Timestamp for when the session was created (ISO 8601).

oneOf.description: Session expiration timestamp (ISO 8601), if concluded naturally or terminated.

expired_at.description: Expiration time for the session or null for active sessions.

authorizations.error_analysis: The main compile error is: 'Cannot find module './MyConfiguration' or its corresponding type declarations.' in src/MyGlobal.ts. authorizations.solution_guidance: 1. If './MyConfiguration' is intended as a sibling file and does not exist, create a minimal MyConfiguration.ts exporting an empty configuration or appropriate environment variables until integration. 3. Ensure that any references to configuration properties in MyGlobal.ts are provided/exported by the configuration module, or mock them for compilation. 4. Authentication provider, decorator, and payload components do not require changes as their compile output and naming match all conventions.

Ensure that MyGlobal.ts can import and use configuration types and values correctly. Do not alter any business/auth logic for this fix.
